v.q: Marco always says please and thank you. He's very ___.
v.e: Polite = good manners, e.g. saying please and thank you.

v.q: Giulia doesn't like talking to new people. She's a bit ___.
v.e: Shy = nervous with people you don't know.

v.q: My uncle always makes us laugh. He's really ___.
v.e: Funny = makes people laugh.

v.q: Sara shares her snacks with everyone. She's ___.
v.e: Generous = happy to give and share.

v.q: He never smiles and he doesn't joke. He's very ___.
v.e: Serious = not joking, not laughing much.

v.q: She answers every question in class without being nervous. She's ___.
v.e: Confident = sure of yourself.

v.q: Which word is the OPPOSITE of polite?
v.e: Rude = bad manners. It's the opposite of polite.

v.q: Which word describes HAIR?
v.e: Curly hair. Tall and slim describe your body.

v.q: Someone who is always happy and smiling is ch_____ . (write the word)
v.e: Cheerful = happy and positive.

v.q: Someone who works very hard is hard-w______ . (write the word)
v.e: Hard-working = puts a lot of effort into work.

v.q: My grandad has no hair. He's ___.
v.e: Bald = with no hair on your head.

v.q: Choose the correct order:
v.e: Size/length comes before colour: long blonde hair.

g.e: Present simple with he/she/it: add -s. She lives.
Questions with he/she/it: Does + base verb.
Negative with I/you/we/they: don't + verb.
Frequency adverbs go AFTER the verb be: He is never late.

o: I often go to the cinema.
I go often to the cinema.
Often I go to cinema the.
g.e: With other verbs, frequency adverbs go BEFORE the verb: I often go.
Verbs ending in -ch add -es: watches.
He/she/it negative: doesn't + base verb.

g.q: What ___ you usually do at the weekend?
g.e: With you: do. What do you usually do…?

s: My best friend is friendly and a bit shy.
I usually go to bed at ten o'clock.
My brother never gets up early.

g.e: Look! = happening now → present continuous: is snowing.
Every day = a habit → present simple.
This term = a temporary situation → present continuous.
Right now → present continuous: are you doing?
Facts and abilities → present simple: she speaks.

g.q: Next Saturday we ___ my grandparents. (it's arranged)
g.e: Fixed future plans → present continuous.
Happening now → is sleeping.

g.q: We ___ (not / go) out tonight – we're tired.
g.e: Present continuous negative: aren't + -ing.

g.q: Which time word goes with the present simple?
g.e: Every weekend = routine → present simple.

g.q: Which time word goes with the present continuous?
g.e: At the moment = now → present continuous.

v.q: Your online ___ tells people about you.
v.e: An online profile = information about you on a website/app.

v.q: I'm ___ in music and photography.
v.e: Interested in = you like it. Interesting = it makes you interested.

v.q: In my free ___ I play video games.
v.e: Free time = time when you aren't working or studying.

v.q: I'm really ___ at drawing.
v.e: Good at + something you do well.

v.q: I'm keen ___ basketball. (preposition)
v.e: Keen on = you like it a lot.

v.q: Which is a hobby?
v.e: A hobby = something you do for fun.

s: I'm learning to play the guitar this year.
At the moment I'm reading a great book.
We're going to the beach on Saturday.

v.q: These jeans are very ___ – they're too big for me!
v.e: Baggy = loose, big.

v.q: You can't wear trainers to a wedding. You need something ___.
v.e: Smart = elegant, for special occasions.

v.q: My grandma's clothes are very ___ – nobody wears that now.
v.e: Old-fashioned = not modern.

v.q: Everyone wants those trainers. They're really ___.
v.e: Fashionable = popular now.

v.q: A T-shirt and jeans are ___ clothes.
v.e: Casual = relaxed, everyday.

v.q: This top is too ___ – I can't move my arms!
v.e: Tight = too small, close to your body.

v.q: A shirt with no pattern is ___.
v.e: Plain = one colour, no pattern.

v.q: A shirt with lines on it is ___.
v.e: Striped = with lines (stripes).

v.q: The opposite of 'tight' is l____ .
v.e: Loose = not tight.

v.q: Clothes for running or the gym are sp____ clothes.
v.e: Sporty = good for sport.

g.q: Which sentence is about a habit?
g.e: Usually = habit → present simple.

g.q: I ___ my school uniform at the moment.
g.e: At the moment → present continuous.
After does: base verb → have.
Never goes before the verb; he → wears.

s: I prefer casual clothes at the weekend.
These shoes are too tight for me.
My dad wears smart clothes for work.

g.e: Buy is irregular: bought.
Go → went.
After didn't: base verb → like.

g.q: ___ you see Marco at the party?
g.e: Past simple questions: Did + subject + base verb.
With yesterday we use the past simple, not the present perfect.
Regular verb: enjoy → enjoyed.
Short verbs ending consonant-vowel-consonant double the last letter: stopped.
Negative: didn't + base verb.

g.q: In the 1980s people ___ big shoulder pads.
g.e: Wear → wore.
Did + base verb: What did you do?

v.q: Hip hop ___ popular in the 1980s.
v.e: Become → became.

v.q: Which word means 'clothes of a particular time'?
v.e: Fashion = the style of clothes popular at a time.

v.q: Which is a time expression for the past?
v.e: Last year = past.

v.q: I saw that film two weeks ___ . (word)
v.e: Two weeks ago = two weeks before now.

s: Last weekend I went shopping with my friends.
Did you watch the match yesterday?
My mum wore baggy jeans in the 1990s.
